text:
mina: We're seeing 5xxs for EU customers since ~10:15 UTC. Requests from EU keep landing in us-west and auth fails (token mismatch). Can repro with a curl. Customer impacted, escalating.
olivia: sorry — can you paste request id + example curl? Are they using regional hostnames or edge host rewrite? :thinking_face:
mina: request-id=abc12345. Example: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <tok>" -H "x-client-region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -v` — returns 502/401 depending on retry.
matt: quick glance at recent deploys: envoys rolled ~1932104400. wondering if header rewrite/route behavior changed. @sara can you check LB/access logs for abc12345?
sara: tailing envoy logs for abc12345 -> upstream_cluster: backend-us-west-1, response_code: 502 then 401 on auth. Route shows an inserted header `x-edge-region: us-west-1`. Attaching small snippet below.
infra-bot: deploy bot: rollout envoy-service v2.14.3 -> completed at 1932104400
matt: that lines up. New filter patch injects `x-edge-region` when `x-client-region` missing or empty. Suspect fallback logic mapping EU -> us-west under certain header-trim conditions.
olivia: can we repro locally w/ --resolve? we should try to force the eu host and see exactly what headers are sent upstream.
matt: repro steps that reproduced the wrong upstream mapping for me:
```
# force eu host and client-region header
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <valid-eu-token>" \
  -H "x-client-region: eu-west-1" \
  --header "Host: eu.api.redwood.example.com" \
  --resolve eu.api.redwood.example.com:443:203.0.113.45 \
  https://eu.api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Observed: Envoy used upstream cluster `backend-us-west-1`, auth service expected EU token -> 401. Also saw an extra `x-edge-region: us-west-1` inserted by route filter.
mina: scope — how many requests affected? Customer reports retries and extra token checks causing billing spike.
sara: metrics: auth 401 spike EU at 10:17–10:50 UTC, latency +170ms due to cross-region RTT; client retries led to ~12% increased token verification calls (billing and load). Trace ids: tracex-777, tracex-778 for samples.
matt: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert header-injection change in Envoy config (remove x-edge-region rewrite) 2) short-circuit fallback to regional backend when `x-client-region` present 3) route-level hack to prefer host header. I started a canary revert.
olivia: please also prepare customer-facing note and open billing review for retry chargebacks. @finance FYI.
matt: reverted the header injection patch at 1932104600 (canary). Early canary traffic now hits eu-backend for traced requests.
sara: confirming: post-revert access logs show upstream_cluster: backend-eu-1 for the traced ids, no 401s, latency normalized. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.
mina: confirmed with customer that calls are now routing correctly — they saw immediate reduction in 5xx/401. Thanks. :pray:
matt: follow-ups: add unit/integration test for header rewrite fallback, add a config lint to catch accidental host_rewrite_literal to wrong region, update runbook with steps to check `x-edge-region` vs `x-client-region`.
olivia: opened tickets: SUP-4852 (customer support), BL-112 (billing investigation), and ENG-2791 (envoy header-rewrite unit tests). Tagging oncall.
mina: thanks team — will update customer on sup ticket and wait for billing confirmation.
matt: postmortem action items and links to logs will follow in ENG channel.
